findings: Implement silent-acceptance hole: _expected_core builds `want` only for OPEN/ATTEMPTS/COLLECTS and the premise loop `elif i < PREFIX_LEN or i >= SUFFIX_START` skips all middle rows not in `want`, so RESTART's recorded decision is never validated; the loop also stops at attest_i, leaving every post-attestation row's decision unchecked (o30-guard-prediction-implement.py ~L89-93, L181-197). Initial-state premise check (~L198-203) ignores collection/collected/attestation/paused and never inspects adapter initial; _core_order validates graph shape but not literal prefix/suffix action identity (self-consistent renamed literals pass). Fixture: deepcopy a valid case, at j=actions.index('source-restart@18') set rows[j]['source_observation']['decision']=rows[j]['adapter_observation']['decision']='source-restart:corrupt' (keeps adapter_decision==decision) -> verdict 'match'/status 'supported'. Control-side inspect_cases catches this via restored ss[i]['decision']; the gap is implement-only. Minimal fix: want[RESTART]='source-restart:ok'; extend the loop over all rows or explicitly scope the tail; tighten initial fields.

Interop miscalibration: 'cross-case-row-graft' expects {'counterexample'} but under implement.inspect_cases grafted rows retain case1 index/action fields -> 'literal-action-mismatch' -> verdict 'incomplete' -> status 'unproved' -> detected=False (control-build ~L160; implement ~L161-172, ~L234-238). Under control-build's own inspect_cases the same mutant yields 'counterexample' via member-driven cx, so run_controls pass/fail depends on which inspect_cases is injected. Fixture: two in-domain cases with different middles, cs[0].update(rows=deepcopy(cs[1]['rows'])) -> got 'unproved'. Minimal fix: resync grafted rows' index/source_action/adapter_action to cs[0]'s schedule so the graft surfaces semantically as 'counterexample', or add 'unproved' to want with a written justification.

Verdict precedence mislabels premise-violating evidence: `if mismatches` precedes `elif premise_failures` (implement ~L213-215), and `want` mixes hypothesis-1 expectations ('collect-open:ok', attempt 'ok') with order-implied semantics. A retained case showing 'collect-open:no-registration' or attempt 'no-registration' (registration premise broken) reports 'counterexample' rather than 'premise_failed', inflating a conditional-domain refutation. Minimal fix: evaluate premise_failures first, or route premise-bound expectations out of `mismatches`.
